whisper.label: Whisper Large-V3
whisper.text:
Hi, I'm Nick Kohler. I'm here at the
Hollow Center's Space Light Alternate
Reality. I'm standing in front of my
piece entitled, Bigger, Brighter, Blinding,
which is a wall of paintings that
incorporate projected light. I'm actually
projecting videos onto the painted
surfaces. You can tell there's a number
of canvases back here behind the
video. And so light is being used as an
art material. It's also the subject
matter here, as a lot of the painted
figures are like turning on and off
lights. They're interacting with fire,
with the Sun itself. So there's a lot
of different ways that that light is
being utilized.
In part, this work is really about the
combination of analog and digital, about
how digital technologies are really
infiltrating our lives as well. In order
to create the videos, I'm using a
collaged process shot on iPhone. And I'm
also like incorporating a home projector
to project the light onto here. So
it's actually about like consumer-grade
technology that's in our lives and it's
available. This all started a number of
years ago. I had the idea to start
attempting to project onto painting. When
it started, it was just still images. But
over time, I developed a video collage
and video art practice and got really
inspired by the idea of actually
bringing movement into the projections
that would go on to the paintings. Inside
my video collages, there's a lot of
different little parts that are moving
and breathing. This movement and breath
really helps bring life into the
paintings themselves through very like
subtle movements. It's almost like you
can look at it and ask like, oh is it
actually moving? Each painting is an
opportunity to explore something new as
well. For example, like in this piece, I'm
actually playing with color theory. I'm
using cyan, yellow, and magenta and
projecting those colors directly on here.
You can see how the colors shift and the
tears that are streaming down the
figure's face, those colors are also
shifting and changing as it goes as
well.
Additionally, there's other processes
that I've gotten to explore. For example,
in this, I've used painted animations
that I document using stop-motion process.
I've actually photographed these
physical paintings on the floor and
some of this piece ends up being like a
frame within a frame within a frame as
you're seeing like the actual canvas and
then the painted animation and then even
the floor is exposed as well. A lot
of these paintings were created in a
time that I was actually like
experimenting with the form and trying
to figure out what I could do with the
projected light on the canvases, what
sort of different processes like
animation and collage I could explore. So
as time has gone on, I've felt more
emboldened to really make some larger
pieces and have them go a little more in
a crazy direction towards light and
technology. So these are kind of just the
beginning of what I've been making in
this series of this body of work. So a
lot of these the scenes that are created
in these paintings are very small scale
and personal and intimate portraits of
people in the same way that the the
technology that I'm using is very it's
consumer grade, it's accessible to
everyone. I wanted to make portraits that
are you know about everyday lives as
well. So these are my my friends, my
roommates. Some of these were actually
made at home during COVID. These two on
the right hand side are my roommates
and which are very domestic scenes were
made with my roommates when we we just
couldn't leave the house because of
lockdowns at the time. There's a third
piece that involved my head being in a
microwave which was a little bit about
the some of the frenetic the chaos and
energy of COVID. But these two are a
little more peaceful and and so they
ended up in this wall as well.
